design_summary.problem: One Mac holds work for two employers (e.g. GitHub orgs 'acme' and 'globex'), an open-source org ('oss-org') and personal projects. orch's single RAG store, session capture, PR digests and task lists currently mix all of them. Content from one employer must never reach a session working for the other; open-source docs should be readable everywhere. Enforcement must be in orchd code, never in prompts.
core_model: A space is the unit of separation. Each space owns bindings: GitHub orgs, local folder roots, web URL prefixes, chat tenants (Slack workspace, Teams tenant), and an outbound term list.

Space kinds: 'public' (readable from every space; only accepts content verified public or under a root the operator declared public; never sessions or agent notes), 'isolated' (one per job; reads itself, public, and any private space it explicitly lists; never another isolated space), 'private' (personal; like isolated, and may read other private spaces it lists).
Two isolated spaces can never read each other. A config that tries is rejected at apply time. Combining two jobs is an explicit operator 'merge' operation.

Every chunk and every orch record (cached PR, event, task, session record) carries exactly one space, or 'quarantine' (readable by no session) when it cannot be placed. Unplaceable content never defaults to public.

Roots nest like GitHub CODEOWNERS: the deepest matching root decides a path's space, and a nested root may only be stricter than every root above it (public < private < isolated; under an isolated root only the same space). Example: ~/code public, ~/code/willesq private, ~/code/company1 isolated.

Placement happens at ingest from the writer (a web page a session ingests takes the session's space). The operator can retag any source; orchd moves its chunks to the new space's collection without re-embedding, deletes them from the old one, and records a sticky override so refreshes keep the new space.

The org that owns a GitHub repo decides its space. Fork parents are ignored. When a checkout's folder root and git remote disagree, the stricter one wins (public < private < isolated); two different isolated spaces disagreeing is a conflict: nothing is indexed and the session gets no space.

Each space gets its own Qdrant collection, plus one for public and one for quarantine. The payload also stores 'space' as a second layer. Searches query only the collections the caller may read and merge them with reciprocal rank fusion.

A caller's space is decided by orchd: the kernel-reported peer PID, walked up the process tree to a harness process registered at SessionStart. A session is pinned to the space of its first cwd for its whole life. Request fields such as cwd never widen access.

A PreToolUse guard (plus CwdChanged logging) records every tool call, extracts its targets (cwd, file paths, cd destinations, git -C, gh repo targets) and refuses calls that reach another isolated space. Moving within the session's own space is allowed. Enforcement is on from the first release.

Defense in layers: orchd memory enforcement (all harnesses), the pre-tool guard, OS sandbox deny rules for other jobs' folders, harness permission rules for file tools, a separate GitHub account per job, and git hooks for outbound terms.

The command log is bounded: deleted 7 days after the session ends (or 7 days after the last event if it never ends), total size cap, refusals kept 90 days, hash-chained, credential-redacted, never indexed into RAG.

Policy changes are drafts until applied by the operator (the user at a terminal or in the app). The policy lives in orch.db as numbered revisions: anyone, agents included, may save a draft; only the operator applies one, naming the revision they reviewed. Callers descended from a harness or from orchd cannot apply. A pending draft, or an applied revision edited in orch.db outside orchd, shows as drift and changes nothing that is enforced.
With no spaces configured, orch behaves exactly as today.

Each enforcement layer (memory filtering, tool guard mode, outbound terms, sandbox rules) has an operator-only switch in the UI and CLI, optionally timed. Switching a layer off is logged and announced in every session's start digest; logging continues while it is off.

A session's liveness comes from the kernel: its pinned harness PID must still exist with the same start time. Idle sessions left open for days stay 'idle', never 'ended'; a process that exits without SessionEnd is marked ended within a minute. 'orch sessions list' shows every session, including running harness processes that have no pin.

Each job space has its own GitHub account (a gh profile directory, GH_CONFIG_DIR) from the start. orchd uses it for that space's docs sync, PR monitoring and reviews. The user logs in to each profile with gh themselves; orch never handles the token.
Spaces cover Claude Code and Codex. No Google harness is in scope.

Per-space harness settings (sandbox denyRead/denyWrite for other jobs' roots, Read/Edit denies, env GH_CONFIG_DIR) are written automatically into each checkout's local, uncommitted settings file; 'orch run <space> -- claude|codex' starts a session with the space's full profile from anywhere.
design_summary.labels: Chunk label = space x trust. trust already exists (assigned server-side by writer). This shape stays compatible with OpenAPPA's audience x trust if an integration is wanted later.

invariants.rule: No read path returns content, URIs or titles from a space outside the caller's readable set.
orchd alone decides a chunk's space and a caller's space. Client-supplied fields (cwd, filters, tags, space) can narrow results but never widen them.
Content that cannot be placed goes to quarantine, never to public or any other space.
Two isolated spaces never read each other. A config that would allow it is rejected and the last applied config stays active.
A session's space is fixed by its first cwd and never changes for the life of the session, including resume, compact and subagents.
Space policy changes take effect only through an operator-only apply. Callers descended from a harness or from orchd are refused.
Outbound terms never appear in logs, transcripts, refusal messages, error messages, the UI or indexed content.
A chunk whose labels_v is not the current policy's is unreadable until relabelled.
Derived content (summaries, session records, task results, files written by a session outside any root) carries the space of what it came from.
With no spaces configured, behavior is identical to today. The existing test suite passes unchanged.
Every cache that holds content or embeddings is keyed by space.
The command log is never indexed into RAG and is readable only by the operator, or by a session for its own events.
While the tool guard is switched on in an enforcing mode, it fails closed: timeout, unreadable pin or unreadable policy means refuse.
A nested root is never less strict than any root above it, and an isolated root never contains a root of a different isolated space.
Retagging moves data and never duplicates it: after a retag, the source exists only in the new space, the total chunk count is unchanged, and no new embeddings were computed.
Enforcement switches are operator-only, every change is logged with time and caller, and while any layer is off every session's start digest says so.

confirmed_by_user.decision: Content can be shared (readable from anywhere) or separated by where the caller runs. Separation is by folder or root location and is verified by orchd code, not by an AI.
Docs (GitHub owner docs, sources) must fall within the separation too, not only sessions.
An open-source GitHub org is readable from anywhere; two employer orgs must never bleed into each other.
Install a pre-tool-use hook that records every command; sessions keep their first directory and cannot circumvent it by changing directory.
The command log is cleaned up, e.g. 7 days after the session ends.
Configuration has a basic setup plus extensive user control in the app UI.
The design must extend to chat feeds later (Teams, Slack channels and DMs).
Use spaces with kinds public/isolated/private (was R-01).
Pin the session's space, not the exact folder; moving within the same space is allowed (was R-02).
One Qdrant collection per space plus public and quarantine collections, with the payload filter as a second layer (was R-03).
Enforcement is on from the first release, not after a log-only period. Every enforcement layer can be switched on and off from the UI so behavior can be isolated when debugging (replaces R-04).
Default guard mode is 'block other jobs'; 'strict' is opt-in; the mode is configurable in the UI (was R-05).
Do not adopt OpenAPPA as a component now; copy its patterns; consider an orch label source later (was R-06).

Content is placed by its writer at ingest: a web page a session ingests takes that session's space. The user can retag any source in the UI, and orchd moves its data to the new space (a move, never a copy) and keeps it there on later refreshes. This keeps the user in control and avoids duplicate data (replaces R-07).

Nested roots are allowed and resolve like GitHub CODEOWNERS: the deepest matching root decides. A nested root may be stricter than the roots above it, never less strict (e.g. ~/code public, ~/code/willesq private, ~/code/company1 isolated). The UI has a validator that shows which roots apply to a directory and the space it resolves to (replaces R-08).
A job (isolated) space may opt in to reading a private space such as personal by listing it in its reads. It is off by default and never extends to another isolated space (was Q-01).
The command log stores the full command text, credential-redacted and capped at 2 KB, plus targets and the decision (was Q-02).
Each job space uses its own GitHub account from the start: orchd's docs sync, PR monitoring and reviews for an isolated space's orgs run only with that space's gh profile (was Q-04).
Queued tasks may explicitly search chat channels in their own space, never DMs; nothing from chat is auto-injected into tasks (was Q-05).
No Google harness (Gemini CLI or Antigravity CLI) is in scope for spaces. Spaces cover Claude Code and Codex; the existing Gemini adapter is left as it is and reported as not covered (was Q-06).
The app shows all spaces at once, labelled, with a one-click screen-share-safe mode that hides everything except a chosen space (was Q-07).
Session content from a session pinned under a public root goes to a configured default space (e.g. personal) and can be retagged later (was Q-08).

Per-space sandbox rules, file-permission denies and GH_CONFIG_DIR reach agent sessions two ways: orch automatically keeps a local settings file in every checkout under a space's roots (no change to how sessions start), and an optional launcher, 'orch run <space> -- claude|codex', starts a session with that space's full profile from any folder (was Q-03, option D).

Keep one Qdrant collection per space (D-10) and accept its measured search cost: 1.5x (2 segments) to 1.9x (default segments) the p95 of one filtered collection, about +15 ms per hybrid search on 40,000 chunks (SP-002, docs/internals/memory.md 'Cost of a collection per space').

config.yaml was removed (settings live in orch.db, PR #142). The spaces policy is stored in orch.db as numbered draft and applied revisions with a content hash; SetSpacesDraft is open to any caller except queued tasks, and drafts record whether the operator saved them; DiffSpaces and ApplySpaces are operator-only and names the reviewed revision, and drift means a pending draft or an applied row that no longer matches its hash. SP-020.2.a3 reworded accordingly.

Accept SP-010's residual audit finding as a documented risk: a process started outside a session's tree under a kept-alive parent can take a new pin in its own directory. Pins grant nothing yet; access by a pin's space is gated on RC-01.

After an SP-011 test wrote to the real orch.db (migrating it from schema 22 to 25 and adding 301 test rows to session_pins), delete only the test rows and keep schema 25; the new tables stay empty until a release uses them.

Tool-call target extraction (SP-013) is best-effort, not a complete analysis of shell. After two security-audit rounds kept finding new ways around it (62 in round 2), fix the broad classes and record the rest as accepted risk. Targets is advisory evidence for the guard; the OS sandbox deny rules (SP-046) and per-job GitHub accounts (SP-063) are the hard boundary, and SP-040 decides how far to trust Targets.

The command log lives in its own SQLite file, toollog.db in orch's data directory, created mode 0600 together with its -wal and -shm files. orch.db's mode is unchanged; the log's growth stays out of orch.db and its backups, and SP-015's total size cap can be measured on the file (was RC-08).

Tool events lost before orchd stores them are recorded where orchd can see them: the intake is a bounded queue, and when it is full the dropped events are counted and written as a 'gap' record in the session's chain. Events lost while orchd is down or slower than the hook's budget are accepted while the guard only logs; SP-041 fails closed once it enforces (was RC-30).
Queued tasks may call RecordToolEvent; their tool calls are logged under the task orchd resolves, never under the session_id the request names (was RC-31).

Admin-merge SP-014 (PR #152) without review while GitHub Actions starts no jobs for the repo (RC-46). DOD-9 is overridden for SP-014: the Linux test job passed at 5c004d8 but the macOS ORT build never ran on the branch; every acceptance item and DOD-1..8 passed independent verification at 5c004d8. Re-run CI on main once Actions works again.

Retention counts a session as ended only when its pin has ended_at and orchd has seen its harness process exit (exited_at); the clock starts at the latest of ended_at, exited_at and the last record. A /clear'd or early-ended session keeps its log (cut to the per-session cap) until its process exits. Deletion happens within one 10-minute sweep after day N (was RC-53).

The total cap removes from the chains that ended first only what expiry would: never refusals under 90 days and never a running session's records, so the file may stay over the cap (logged). Retention (3d/7d/30d) and the total cap stay Sensitive settings read at orchd start. The per-session cap (50 MB, per chain) becomes a setting too (SP-073) (was RC-54).

Command log tamper evidence is strengthened: each anchor (seq, hash) is also copied into orch.db and verify compares the two, and a queued task's chain is anchored when the task reaches a terminal state (SP-073) (was RC-42).

Tool events from a harness process with no pin are logged in a chain keyed by that process (PID and start time) instead of being dropped; retention ends the chain when the process exits (SP-073) (was RC-43).

Refusals and other guard decisions are never dropped from the command log: queue room is reserved for them, and only ordinary logged events may drop with a gap record when a share is full (SP-041.1.a4) (was RC-45).
Memory reads are never widened by a session pin's space until the enforcing guard (SP-041) stops a session from starting a harness outside its process tree: SP-025 depends on SP-041 (was RC-01).

A caller resolved as the operator by process tree alone does not get operator-scope memory reads: SP-025 requires evidence of a real operator (a controlling terminal, or Orch.app); otherwise the caller reads public only. A process that left its session's tree therefore loses operator reads (was RC-26).

Turning off the tool hooks (pre-tool-use, cwd-changed) is an SP-070 enforcement switch: operator-only, logged with time and caller, and announced in every session's start digest; orch settings cannot turn them off silently (was RC-32).

Confirmed as built in SP-017: a resume moves a pin only to a fresh top-level harness whose directory places into the pin's space; an in-process /resume of another process's session is refused and its events go to the process's own pin; a 'claude --resume' started in another space's directory runs unpinned (was RC-47).
The dependency mvdan.cc/sh/v3 (pure Go, BSD-3-Clause) is kept for parsing shell commands in tool-call target extraction, with command substitution, globbing and ~user lookups disabled (was RC-35).
Codex pinning is checked by the user after the next release (RC-57), not by a new acceptance item (was RC-02).

Before the guard enforces, orchd identifies a connection's peer by a kernel token (LOCAL_PEERTOKEN on macOS, SO_PEERPIDFD on Linux) rather than its PID alone, so a PID reused after a process handed off its socket cannot be mistaken for the original peer; a peer that cannot be identified gets no space, never a default (SP-041.1.a5) (was RC-03).

Connection resolution has no cost bound of its own: SP-011.2's 5 ms bound is retired, and the cost is covered by the tool hooks' 20 ms budget and SP-041's decision-latency check (p99 < 50 ms). TestResolveCost's bound is removed as a follow-up (RC-58) (was RC-28).

A queued task reads and writes the space of the session that dispatched it; a task the operator dispatched takes the placement of its working directory; a task orchd cannot find (not tracked by its runner) gets no space and reads public only (SP-025.1.a8) (was RC-25).

Redaction stays best-effort and is maintained, not systematically extended: concrete misses are fixed with regression tests as they are found, and the OS sandbox (SP-046) and per-job GitHub accounts (SP-063) are the boundary, as D-28 decided for target extraction (was RC-44).

The session list's unpinned rows skip processes whose parent is a harness (subprocesses that keep the harness's name) and known daemons such as Codex's app-server; top-level harness processes are listed even without a TTY (RC-59) (was RC-49).
Pins are not made to survive orchd restarts on Linux; orch runs on macOS (was RC-04).

Under a public root, content from a checkout with no verifiable public remote (not on GitHub, or no remote) is quarantined until the operator retags it or declares that folder public; a public root alone is not proof (SP-030.1 new item) (was RC-05).
The operator confirms a specific GitHub node ID for an org binding (org=node_id), and 'orch spaces diff' shows the old, new and seen node IDs (RC-61) (was RC-06).
Every GitHub ingestion path (docs sync, sources, the review watcher, PR monitoring) re-checks the org binding before writing, and a long sync re-checks between repos (SP-023 new item) (was RC-07).

Each space gets its own TMPDIR from the launcher and per-checkout settings, with other spaces' temp dirs denied; the combined root settings.local.json (sandbox on, unsandboxed commands off, Read denies) is tested from a subfolder with Read, Grep, Glob and Edit. The shared /tmp stays a documented residual (SP-046 new items) (was RC-09).

All four SP-063 follow-ups become planned work in SP-074: scopes and PR watching for profile-only orgs; refusing GitHub calls a space's profile cannot read, with stricter gh_config_dir checks; the repo picker and PR-outcome tracker using the space's profile; a GitHub API quota cap per isolated account (was RC-10).

SP-073, SP-040 and SP-070 are worked in parallel by three independent agent sessions, each in its own worktree and draft PR, overriding session_procedure step 2 (one feature, one session at a time) for these three only; their dependencies are done and their code barely overlaps. To avoid id clashes each reserves a block of reconvene ids: SP-073 RC-66..RC-75, SP-040 RC-76..RC-85, SP-070 RC-86..RC-95. New confirmed_by_user decisions are recorded by the coordinating session. Whichever PR merges later is rebased onto main (plan file, orch.db migration numbers, regenerated proto stubs).

SP-044's outbound terms hook check is best-effort static reading of shell, like D-28; SP-045's git hooks and per-job accounts are the boundary for git. The residual classes in RC-117 (MCP tools, scripts and programs that run git, interpreters, curl, forged tracking refs) stay accepted risk. The baseline is loosened in SP-044: a gh write without -R counts only the repo gh would use (its default repo, else the checkout's base remote), not every remote; plain variables ($PWD, $USER, $HOME) and literal assignments made earlier in the same command are read instead of refused; more harmless 'git -c' keys are allowed. Making the rules configurable (baseline rules switchable by id, user-added stricter rules, CLI and app, stored in orch.db, operator-only) is SP-075.

reconvene.topic: Gate pin-based access on the tool guard
reconvene.detail: SP-011 and SP-025 must not grant memory reads by a pin's space until SP-041 stops a session from starting a harness outside its tree, or until there is stronger evidence of a real top-level harness (kernel executable path, session and tty checks). Today one command can start a fake 'claude' under a kept-alive shell and pin it in another directory (accepted risk, D-26).
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: SP-025 depends on SP-041; see D-38 and SP-025.1.a6.

reconvene.topic: Codex SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks
reconvene.detail: orch's Codex install registers no SessionStart or SessionEnd hook, so Codex sessions are never pinned. Proposal: register orch-hook session-start and session-end for Codex (D-20 covers Codex). Update 2026-11-09 (SP-012 session): the current install code already registers SessionStart and SessionEnd (and the other eventSlugs) in ~/.codex/hooks.json, checked by TestCodexHooksUnchanged; SP-012 keeps them in its Codex event map. If Codex sessions are still unpinned, the installed hooks.json probably predates that or its hooks are untrusted; `orch install --target codex` (dry run) shows the difference.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: checked after the next release; see D-43 and RC-57.

reconvene.topic: Bind the peer PID to its connection (proposed SP-011 acceptance item)
reconvene.detail: NearestAncestor trusts its starting PID; a peer that forks, hands its socket to a child and exits leaves its PID free for reuse under another space's harness. Bound the walk by the accept time, or identify the peer by kernel token (LOCAL_PEERTOKEN, SO_PEERPIDFD). Not found must mean no space, never a default.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: identify peers by kernel token before enforcement; see D-44 and SP-041.1.a5.

reconvene.topic: SP-020 audit lows
reconvene.detail: Prune old draft revisions; normalise roots (NFC/NFD, symlinks) and web prefixes the way enforcement will match; clearer refusal when a bare node/bun/deno above 'orch' makes orchd refuse the operator, and don't count doubled '/' toward the depth limit; a session can keep saving drafts so the operator's apply is always stale; 'orch status' should say nothing is readable when the newest apply fails to verify; resolve root symlinks before nesting checks; transient changed_outside_orchd during an apply.

reconvene.topic: SP-022 lows
reconvene.detail: The repo lookup cache and its 30-a-minute budget are shared by agents and the operator (timing side channel; agents can starve the operator). Agent-supplied paths reach the handoff checkout reader, which has no timeout or concurrency cap. Paths match case-insensitively but URL paths case-sensitively, and IDN/punycode hosts are not unified. An applied policy binding both spellings of a web prefix to different spaces fails to load at the next orchd start.

reconvene.topic: SP-010 lows
reconvene.detail: The PinSession comment in orchd.proto says 'live pin' though the rule also applies to an ended pin; the registry lock is held while placement waits on GitHub (up to 10 s); a harness can claim a not-yet-pinned session ID first (denial of service only); the harness start time is read just after the walk; a session can end its own pin early.

reconvene.topic: Which space a queued task reads and writes
reconvene.detail: SP-011 resolves a task's process to its live run (task ID, directory, session) from the process tree; a reported orch-task-id only marks a caller as a task. No feature decides a task's space (the dispatching session's pin, the placement of its cwd, or a space named at dispatch), and a task whose run orchd is not tracking (a verification run, a run in another worker) has no record and so resolves to no space. Decide before SP-025 enforces reads.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: the dispatcher's space; see D-46 and SP-025.1.a8.

reconvene.topic: A process that left its session's tree resolves to the operator
reconvene.detail: SP-011 resolves a caller with no harness above it as the operator, the widest result. A session process that double-forks, or starts a process through launchctl submit, open or osascript, before orchd accepts its connection, gets that result without a fake harness or a pin. This is wider than the D-26 detached-harness case. SP-025 must not grant operator-level memory reads by resolution alone until SP-041 (or kernel evidence such as audit tokens) covers it.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: operator-scope reads need a terminal or Orch.app; see D-39 and SP-025.1.a7.

reconvene.topic: SP-011 audit lows
reconvene.detail: The resolved session ID is 'a session of this harness process' (subagent and /clear pins share the process), not necessarily the caller's own; SP-016 and SP-017 must not key per-session data on it without telling them apart (documented in docs/internals/daemon.md, Caller sessions). reconvene.topic: SP-012 audit lows for the command log store
reconvene.detail: The SP-012 security audit found no critical/high/medium issues. Its lows L2-L4 apply once SP-014 stores events: cap each RecordToolEvent string field (e.g. 4 KiB; only gRPC's 4 MiB bounds them now); treat events from unresolved callers (callerNone) as untrusted or drop them, and bound the intake (a buffered channel that drops when full, with a count) so a flood cannot build up memory; redact tool_input with the ingest scrubber before storing it and never log the request. L1 (uncapped hook stdin) was fixed with an 8 MiB cap.
reconvene.note: Done in SP-014 (PR #152), 2026-11-09: fields other than tool_input capped at 4 KiB and unknown protobuf fields refused; operator, unresolved and untracked-task events are counted and not stored; the intake is bounded by count, bytes and a per-process share, with drops written as gap records; commands and every text field are redacted before storage, and requests are never logged.

reconvene.topic: How the guard reads Targets: ancestors, prefixes and opaque calls
reconvene.detail: From the SP-013 security review. (1) A path or prefix that is an ancestor of another space's root (grep -r ~/code, find ~/code -exec ...) reaches into that space; SP-040 must treat it so, since Targets reports such paths as plain paths. (2) Targets flags many forms opaque (eval, python -c, unknown variables, git -c outside an allowlist, a cd in a loop, ...). SP-040 must decide what 'block other jobs' mode does with an opaque call, and should measure how often ordinary agent commands come back opaque before choosing. (3) Targets stops at 100 ms or 512 targets and flags the call opaque; with INV-13 the enforcing guard must refuse when that happens, not allow.

reconvene.topic: Known limits of tool-call target extraction
reconvene.detail: Accepted for SP-013 under D-28 and documented in docs/internals/hooks.md: paths a program computes at run time (compiled tools, interpreter logic beyond literal paths, commands found on PATH whose scripts are not read) are not seen; string arguments of unknown programs and commands inside unknown wrappers are walked only as a guess, so what cannot be read there does not make the call opaque; a single-component link created by archive extraction, cp or mv and used by bare name in the same call is not flagged; the parser follows bash, and of zsh only two-operand cd, $var[...] subscripts, cdpath and running the last pipeline stage in the current shell are handled; ssh host aliases count as GitHub only when the alias contains 'github' (~/.ssh/config is not read), and ssh commands are walked as if run in this machine's $HOME; whether Codex fires PreToolUse for write_stdin is unverified (Targets flags it opaque). See RC-38 for what cannot be verified at all.

reconvene.topic: What the tool guard cannot verify today: candidates for more security layers
reconvene.detail: Recorded at the user's request (2026-11-09) to revisit when adding layers. Targets reads only the tool input, so none of these can be verified from it: (1) code a command runs that is not in the input: git hooks, Makefile recipes, npm/package scripts, test runners, compiled tools, and scripts found on PATH; (2) shell state from earlier calls or the user's rc files: functions and aliases Claude Code's shell snapshot loads, exported variables, shopt/setopt options, a cwd changed in a previous call; (3) variables and config that make tools run code or change where they read: PAGER/EDITOR/VISUAL/LESSOPEN/PS4-style variables, ~/.gitconfig and repo .git/config (aliases, hooks, url rewrites), ssh config host aliases; (4) paths computed at run time by interpreters or tools, and files changed by earlier calls or by other processes between check and use; (5) zsh-only syntax, since the parser follows bash; (6) GitHub targets named indirectly: numeric repo IDs, GraphQL, search, org-wide listings, and API calls made by MCP servers or tools themselves; (7) MCP servers' own semantics (relative paths resolve against the server's project, not the cwd); (8) unverified harness facts: whether Codex fires PreToolUse for write_stdin and exec_command's shell field, and whether hook payloads ever omit the tool input. Candidate layers: OS sandbox deny rules per job (SP-046), per-job GitHub accounts (SP-063), outbound-term git hooks (SP-044/SP-045), a guard 'strict' mode that refuses opaque calls (D-12), running jobs under separate macOS users or containers, and auditing the command log for opaque calls.

reconvene.topic: SP-013 audit lows and ordinary commands that come back opaque
reconvene.detail: From the third SP-013 security review (all high and medium findings fixed). Left as low: (1) os.Lstat/Stat can block on an autofs or stale network mount, and the 100 ms deadline cannot interrupt a blocked syscall; (2) ordinary forms that are opaque by design and may matter for SP-040's opaque policy: 'for f in *.go; do ... "$f"; done' (loop variable), scripts that start with cd "$(dirname "$0")/..", '| xargs', 'make test V=1', backticks inside a double-quoted commit message (bash runs them), 'echo {1..10}'; (3) npm/package.json/pyproject scripts and 'python -m <module>' code are not followed (RC-38). Decide in SP-040 whether to model any of (2) before the guard enforces. Also: the table case 'Agent has no targets' asserts /etc/x is absent, which is only meaningful on Linux (on macOS /etc resolves to /private/etc); switch it to a path such as /z/x (noted by the SP-013 verifier).

reconvene.topic: SP-014 audit lows for the command log
reconvene.detail: Accepted as Low in the five SP-014 security reviews: (1) Open checks the path with Lstat, then Chmod and SQLite reopen it by name (a same-user process could swap it; use O_NOFOLLOW and Fchmod), and the data directory is 0755; (2) gap records can land slightly out of order relative to an owner's already-queued later events (counts stay right), and drops recorded under a claimed session are not taken by that session's End; (3) the writer's chain-head cache is not pruned for tasks or sessions that never send SessionEnd; (4) every event whose hook names a session other than the caller's pin costs two orch.db reads on the single writer goroutine, so a hook doing that on purpose slows storage for everyone; (5) four flooding harness processes can still fill the whole queue (each may take a quarter); (6) VerifyToolLog loads a whole chain into memory; (7) redaction of a large RAG document costs about 0.3-0.6 s per MiB on adversarial input (linear).

reconvene.topic: How strong the command log's tamper evidence should be
reconvene.detail: SP-014's chain detects modified, deleted and reordered records, but the anchors live in toollog.db itself: records removed after the last anchor, or a chain rewritten from its first record, cannot be detected, and task chains are never anchored (tasks send no SessionEnd). Options: copy each anchor's (seq, hash) into orch.db or another store the guard protects (SP-042), anchor a task's chain when it reaches a terminal state, or accept file-level tamper evidence and rely on the OS sandbox (SP-046) to keep sessions out of the file.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: anchors copied into orch.db and task chains anchored at their end; see D-35 and SP-073.

reconvene.topic: Tool events of unpinned sessions are not logged
reconvene.detail: SP-014 stores only events orchd can attribute to a pinned session or a running task; events from a harness with no pin (started before the hooks were installed, or whose PinSession failed), from the operator, or from a task orchd cannot find are counted by caller kind and dropped. Decide whether SP-017's 'unpinned' sessions should get a chain keyed by their harness process.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: unpinned processes get a chain of their own; see D-36 and SP-073.

reconvene.topic: Review the broader redaction rules shared with RAG ingestion
reconvene.detail: SP-014 added rules to internal/redact used by docs sync, sources, handoffs, summaries and Ingest: AWS secrets after a space or JSON-escaped quote, Authorization with %20, URL user info, *PASSWORD/SECRET/TOKEN/API_KEY* environment assignments, 'password=' or quoted 'password: "x"', query secrets, X-Api-Key/Cookie headers, curl/wget -u, mysql -p, docker-style 'login -p', long --token values, npm/GitLab/Google/Slack refresh tokens. More aggressive rules (any 'login -p', any --password, unquoted YAML password, an unterminated private key) apply to the command log only (redact.RedactCommand), because they damaged ordinary docs in review. Residual false positives in docs are possible (e.g. 'password = example', GH_TOKEN_FILE=...), and a page with more than 25 matches is skipped as a keystore (redact.Threshold). Review whether the shared set is right for RAG. Redaction is pattern-based and so best-effort: each of the five SP-014 review rounds found further credential forms, all fixed with regression tests in internal/redact/redact_test.go. Known remaining command-log gaps (Low): a password starting with '-' after -p (kept so the rule does not swallow the next flag), unquoted YAML values containing spaces or a backslash, and targets JSON redacted with the shared rules only (a path-shaped password could survive in targets). Decide whether to keep extending patterns or treat the OS sandbox and per-job accounts as the boundary, as D-28 did for target extraction.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: maintain, with the sandbox and per-job accounts as the boundary; see D-47. Documentation note tracked in RC-60.

reconvene.topic: A session can hide what it ran by flooding its own queue share

reconvene.topic: A resume moves a pin only to a fresh top-level harness in the same space
reconvene.detail: SP-017 moves a pin on SessionStart source=resume only when the new harness process could take a new pin of its own (not inside another session, holding no pin, not an orphan, under 5 minutes old, kernel-verified cwd) and its directory places into the pin's space. orchd cannot tell an in-process /resume from an agent calling PinSession itself to take a dead session of its space and write that session's command log (SP-017 security review, round 1 medium), so an in-process /resume of another process's session is refused and that session's tool events go to the process's own pin. A 'claude --resume' started in a directory of another space is also refused and that session runs unpinned. Confirm, or decide another rule.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: confirmed as built; see D-41.

reconvene.topic: What counts as session activity
reconvene.detail: 'active' vs 'idle' uses the latest of pinned_at, resumed_at and the session's last tool event in the command log. Other hook events (UserPromptSubmit, Stop) do not reach orchd with a session identity, and with the command log off activity is the pin's own times. Refusals count events with decision 'refused' (toollog.DecisionRefused), which SP-041 must write for a refused call.

reconvene.topic: Which processes the session list shows as unpinned
reconvene.detail: Unpinned rows are every claude, codex or gemini process of the user with no live pin, by kernel name as procstat.FindByName does (plus node/bun/deno and version-named binaries by program). On this Mac that includes Codex's app-server daemon processes and every claude subprocess that keeps the name, not only interactive sessions. Decide whether to filter (e.g. only processes with a TTY, or skip children of a harness).
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: skip harness children and known daemons; see D-48 and RC-59.

reconvene.topic: SP-017 audit lows
reconvene.detail: Accepted as Low in two SP-017 security reviews and documented in docs/internals/daemon.md: (1) the detached fake harness (D-26) can also resume a dead or ended session of the space whose directory it starts in and write its command log, until SP-041; (2) a process detached from its session resolves as the operator (RC-26) and sees every space and directory in ListSessions; (3) pins are not capped per harness process and never pruned until SP-015, so sweeps and the list read every pin while holding the registry lock, and an agent can insert many copied pins; options: cap pins per process, throttle list-triggered sweeps, sweep by process; (4) the per-connection pin cache is not dropped when a resume moves a pin: ListSessions checks the pin still names the caller's process, and any future session-scoped read of the command log (INV-12) must do the same; (5) a resume between a sweep and its endToolLog leaves an end record in a live chain (re-anchored at the next end).

reconvene.topic: Sessions of subagents and /clear stay listed until their process exits
reconvene.detail: Pins a subagent or an earlier /clear session copied share the harness process; those that get no SessionEnd show as active or idle rows of their own until the process exits. Consider listing only a process's current session, or marking copied pins.

reconvene.topic: When retention counts a session as ended
reconvene.detail: SP-015 treats a session as ended only when its pin has ended_at and the liveness sweep has seen its harness process gone (new session_pins.exited_at, migration 0027); the clock starts at the latest of ended_at, exited_at and the chain's last record. Reason: docs/internals/daemon.md already promised that ending a pin early (any process in the session can call EndSession) does not expire a running process's log, and the audit showed an early end would otherwise delete a log the moment its process exits. Consequences to confirm: a session ended by /clear keeps its log (cut to 50 MB) until the harness process exits; a normal SessionEnd counts from the exit seen up to a minute later; a session whose exit is not yet seen counts as running; sweeps run every 10 minutes, so 'deleted at day N' happens within 10 minutes after it.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: confirmed as built; see D-33.

reconvene.topic: Total cap and settings for the command log
reconvene.detail: The total cap (sessions.command_log.max_total_mb, default 500, 100-100000) removes from the chains that ended first only what expiry would: never refusals under 90 days and never a running session's records, so the file can stay over the cap (orchd logs it). The spec's 'deletes the oldest ended sessions first' is read that way after the audit showed whole-chain deletion let a flood erase other sessions' refusals. The 50 MB cap is per chain (a process holding several /clear'd sessions can keep several) and a constant, not a setting. Retention (3d/7d/30d) and the cap are Sensitive settings in a new 'Command log' section, read when orchd starts; another value keeps the default.
reconvene.note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-10: confirmed, with the per-session cap made a setting; see D-34 and SP-073.

reconvene.topic: SP-015 audit lows and documented limits
reconvene.detail: Accepted as Low over three SP-015 security reviews and documented in docs/internals/daemon.md: (1) expiry and the cap delete a chain in one statement, so a very large delete holds the write turn and the writer's queue can overflow into a gap (chunk deletes); (2) task chains look ended when no runner exists (at startup before the worker starts, or with the worker off); (3) every sweep scans all records to size chains (keep sizes in a side table); (4) wall-clock jumps move expiry; (5) the one-time VACUUM converting an SP-014 log runs before orchd serves and is retried on every start after a failure; (6) the writer builds records inside its write transaction, so slow work added to toolRecord would hold the write turn; (7) a pruned head written into the file by hand still excuses a chain deleted whole, or a prefix up to a record whose hash is copied: verify shows the cut and orchd's log has no matching line; (8) flooding the log (busy sessions, or an agent) pushes ended sessions' records other than refusals out early through the total cap; (9) a running chain's refusals are never cut, so a refusal flood is bounded only once its session ends.

reconvene.topic: Session pins are still never pruned
reconvene.detail: SP-015 deletes command-log records but keeps every session_pins row, because retention counts from ended_at/exited_at and a resume continues a deleted chain from its pruned head. RC-50 (3) remains: sweeps and ListSessions read every pin. Proposal: delete a pin (and its pruned head) once its chain has no records left and it ended more than 90 days ago, or cap pins per harness process.

reconvene.topic: Check that Codex sessions are pinned
reconvene.detail: After the next release is installed, open a Codex session, then run `orch install --target codex` (dry run; it should show no difference in ~/.codex/hooks.json) and `orch sessions list`: the Codex session should be listed with a space, not as unpinned. If it is unpinned, the installed hooks.json predates the SessionStart/SessionEnd registration or Codex does not trust the hooks.

reconvene.topic: Remove TestResolveCost's 5 ms bound
reconvene.detail: D-45 retires SP-011.2's per-connection cost bound. Drop the bound from TestResolveCost (internal/daemon) or turn it into a reported measurement, and say in docs/internals/daemon.md that the hook budget and SP-041's latency check cover the cost. Small; can ride along with SP-041.

reconvene.topic: Filter unpinned rows in the session list
reconvene.detail: D-48: ListSessions' unpinned rows should skip processes whose parent is a harness process and known daemons (Codex app-server), keeping top-level harnesses even without a TTY. Small change in internal/daemon/liveness.go (unpinned) with a test; can ride along with SP-016 or SP-051.

reconvene.topic: Say redaction is best-effort in the docs
reconvene.detail: D-47: state in docs/internals (ingestion and command log sections) that redaction is pattern-based and best-effort, and that the OS sandbox and per-job accounts are the boundary; list the known gaps from RC-44. Docs only.

reconvene.topic: Confirm a specific GitHub node ID
reconvene.detail: D-51: --confirm-github-org takes org=node_id, and 'orch spaces diff' shows old, new and seen node IDs for each binding. SP-021 is done; this can ride along with SP-053 (advanced editors) or SP-074.

reconvene.topic: What the weekly command-log summary counts
reconvene.detail: SP-016's 'orch spaces log summary' counts directory moves only from cwd-changed events: Codex sends none, and a Bash 'cd' (a target SP-013 extracts) or a tool call reaching another space's files is not counted as a move. Queued tasks have no space until SP-023 and are summed under '' with sessions pinned with no policy and chains whose pin is gone; their moves are not compared. A move counts as 'into another space' when a session started in the new directory would be pinned to a different space under the policy applied now, not the revision recorded on the event (policy_rev), and placement answers GitHub lookups from the cache only, so an uncached repo is placed by the owner its remote names and may differ from what PinSession would decide. Decide whether the summary should count calls whose targets reach another space (likely once SP-040 decides per call), place by the recorded revision, and count cache misses as unplaced.

reconvene.topic: Replies a client never reads (second SP-016 audit, residual)
reconvene.detail: gRPC keeps a unary reply in memory until the client reads it, after the handler returns. SP-016 caps an agent's ListToolEvents page at 512 KiB, allows one read per chain at a time, and caps every orchd connection at 128 open calls (grpc.MaxConcurrentStreams, maxStreamsPerConn). A local process that opens many connections and sends calls without reading replies can still make orchd hold them; this applies to every agent-callable RPC with large replies (GetDocument, ListDocs, Search, ListToolEvents), not only the command log. Options: cap connections per process in peerCredentials, a server-wide budget for unsent replies, or accept it with the OS sandbox and orchd's restart as the bound.

reconvene.topic: Which of a harness process's sessions a session may read
reconvene.detail: ListToolEvents gives a session only the current session of its harness process (the pin caller resolution picks, RC-27), and only while that is still the pin its connection resolved: after /clear, or once a subagent's pin is newer, an earlier session's log is readable only by the operator, and an older connection is refused until it reconnects (the CLI always reconnects). The command log's writer already treats sessions of one process as related (resolveClaim). Confirm, or let a session read every chain pinned to its own harness process.

reconvene.topic: SP-016 audit lows and notes
reconvene.detail: From the two SP-016 security reviews, accepted as Low or informational: (1) a process reparented out of the harness tree (launchd, open, osascript) counts as the operator, as documented under Caller sessions; reading the command log makes that bypass more rewarding, and the OS sandbox (SP-046) is the boundary; (2) a session that runs 'orch spaces log' puts its own redacted log into its transcript, which the session-end summary ingests into RAG; the text is the session's own commands, already in its transcript, but decide whether INV-12 should refuse the table inside a harness; (3) 'orch spaces log verify' prints the owner and problem details without cell(); (4) the CLI buffers every page and shares one 30 s deadline, so a very large log can time out having printed nothing (flush per page or stream); (5) the shared flush is best effort (a reader joining a running flush may miss events taken just before it called); (6) the summary's placing deadline cannot interrupt a stat that blocks (an autofs or dead network mount under /net or /Volumes); consider skipping non-local filesystems. (7) no test pins grpc.MaxConcurrentStreams in newGRPCServer, so a refactor could drop it silently; (8) two 'orch spaces log' runs from one session at the same moment: the second is refused (ResourceExhausted) with no retry.

reconvene.topic: Flaky TestWatchTasksStreamsSnapshotChangesAndTicks hides internal/daemon from make cover
reconvene.detail: TestWatchTasksStreamsSnapshotChangesAndTicks (internal/daemon/taskwatch_test.go) fails about one run in five on main at ea0b147 with 'WatchTasks ended with context canceled' (also under -race); SP-073 does not touch it. scripts/cover.sh appends a package's profile only when its tests pass, so when this test flakes the whole internal/daemon package silently drops out of the per-file gate and make cover still prints 'All files >= 80%'. Fix the test (a send racing the client's cancel), and make cover.sh fail, or at least warn, when a package's tests fail. Also seen on PR #165: TestTargetsAuditRound2Scripts (internal/spaces/targets_audit2_test.go:153, 'fan-out sources', 6000 sourced scripts under a time budget) failed CI run 43049750035's first attempt with 'neither opaque nor reaching .../otherco' and passed on the re-run and locally; the budget-dependent case is likely flaky under CI load.
reconvene.note: The flaky-test part was fixed on 2026-11-11 by https://github.com/willesq/orchestrator/pull/168 (fixed on the user's instruction); see RC-92. Still open: scripts/cover.sh silently drops a package whose tests fail, so make cover can print 'All files >= 80%' with that package missing. TestTargetsAuditRound2Scripts' budget-dependent case is also unaddressed.

reconvene.topic: Which task states anchor a task's command log chain
reconvene.detail: SP-073 anchors a queued task's chain once its ledger status is anything but pending or in_progress (queue.Unsettled): complete, failed (a timed-out run is failed with 'timed out after ...'), cancelled, and also blocked and interrupted, and only when no run of it is live. orchd follows the ledger through the task hub, which takes one of its 16 watcher slots (maxWatchers) for good; every retention sweep also anchors any task chain left open whose task is terminal. Confirm the states, and whether internal subscribers should be exempt from maxWatchers.

reconvene.topic: Limits of the orch.db copies of command log anchors (SP-073 audit lows and notes)
reconvene.detail: From the two SP-073 security reviews, accepted as Low or informational: (1) toollog.db and orch.db belong to the same user, so the copies are defense in depth against edits to toollog.db, not against a process that can write both; (2) at every open orchd copies anchors toollog.db holds that orch.db lacks (repairs a crash between the two writes), so an anchor only in toollog.db is reported only until the next orchd start; copies are never replaced; (3) pruned heads are copied only the first time (logs from before SP-073 are trusted as they were), and a cut copy lost in a crash or dropped past 10,000 waiting makes verify report that chain until a later cut moves the copy past it; a stronger fix writes the cut to orch.db before the toollog.db delete commits and lets verify accept a copy ahead of the file when the records between still link; (4) verify works per owner, so a chain deleted whole shows only when that owner is verified (consider 'orch spaces log verify --all' over orch.db's owners); (5) copy-at-open logs only how many anchors it copied, not whose; (6) a verify racing a retention cut is retried once and can still, rarely, report a cut not yet copied (never a false pass).

reconvene.topic: Cap on unpinned harness process chains
reconvene.detail: D-36 logs a harness process holding no pin in its own chain. A running chain is never expired nor cut for the total cap, and any process named like a harness counts, so SP-073 allows at most 8 such chains open at once (maxProcessChains, a constant): events of further unpinned processes are dropped and counted, logged as one total per liveness sweep, until one exits or is pinned (a pinned process's chain is ended and its place freed). Worst case the process chains hold 8 x max_session_mb. Confirm 8, or make it a setting, and decide whether the drop log should name the processes.

reconvene.topic: Session list rows do not name an unpinned process's log chain
reconvene.detail: ListSessions shows an unpinned process's tool events, refusals and last event, but SessionInfo has no field for its chain ID (process:<pid>-<start ns>); 'orch spaces log process:<pid>' resolves the latest chain of that PID instead. A log_owner field was not added to the proto, to avoid regenerating the Go and Swift stubs while SP-040, SP-070 and SP-073 run in parallel (D-55). Add it (and show process chains in the app, SP-054) when convenient.

reconvene.topic: The guard does not judge what a cwd contains in block-other-jobs
reconvene.detail: SP-040 judges a cd_dest, path, git dir or glob prefix that contains another job's root as reaching that job, but the call's cwd only in strict mode. Otherwise every call of a session started under a public root such as ~/code (which holds every job's root) would be refused. So in block-other-jobs a command that searches its cwd by default (grep -r x, rg x, find, du, tar) run with cwd ~/code is allowed, and the OS sandbox (SP-046) is the boundary. Options: keep this; or refuse such calls when the command is a known recursive reader with no path argument (needs Targets to report it); or pin public-root sessions out of ancestor cwds.

reconvene.topic: block-other-jobs allows opaque calls (RC-36 (2))
reconvene.detail: SP-040's block-other-jobs mode allows an opaque call whose known targets stay out of other jobs (rule opaque_unverified, logged for audit); strict refuses it (opaque_strict); calls opaque because Targets hit a limit or had no absolute cwd or home are refused in both enforcing modes (analysis_limit, RC-36 (3)). Measured before choosing: 0 of the 46 recorded Claude Code and Codex PreToolUse fixtures (internal/hook/testdata/payloads) come back opaque; the real command log on this Mac is empty because the tool hooks are not wired yet (RC-33), so the rate on real agent work is unmeasured. Re-measure from the command log once the hooks run (counts of opaque_unverified per space via orch spaces log) before SP-041 enforces, and confirm or tighten.

reconvene.topic: Paths that contain another job's root are refused
reconvene.detail: Per RC-36 (1), block-other-jobs refuses a path, cd destination, git dir or glob prefix that contains another isolated space's root (grep -r ~/code, cd ~/code && rg x, find / ..., ls ~/code), because Targets cannot tell a recursive reader from a listing. This adds friction for sessions under a public root (cd ~/code before a git clone, ls ~/code). Confirm, or decide to allow a listing-only set of commands (ls, cd alone) once Targets can report it.

reconvene.topic: What SP-041 must do around Decide
reconvene.detail: From the SP-040 security reviews. (1) The zero GuardPolicy means 'no spaces configured' and allows everything (INV-10); SP-041 must refuse (INV-13) when the policy snapshot cannot be read or does not validate, never pass the zero value. (2) NewGuardPolicy resolves root and protected-path symlinks once; SP-041 must rebuild it when the policy, a root or its links change (replay is exact only against the same snapshot). (3) A missing pin refuses in enforcing modes (pin_missing); decide how queued tasks without a session pin are judged. (4) Limit reasons are matched by message text; TestLimitReasonsMatchTargets checks forceOpaque reasons and that every listed reason still exists, but a new limit raised with plain opaque() would not be flagged; consider a typed limit flag in ToolTargets. (5) Pass EventCwdChanged only for cwd-changed: every other kind, including an empty one, is enforced.

reconvene.topic: SP-040 audit lows and design choices
reconvene.detail: (1) In strict mode a private root symlinked into another non-public space is placed by the deepest root only, so unreadable_space can judge by the wrong space (never lets one job reach another; otherJobHolds covers isolated spaces). (2) Self-protection covers file-tool writes (Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, apply_patch); shell writes to protected paths (>, tee, sed -i, cp, mv) are SP-042's, since Targets does not tell writes from reads. (3) An unknown guard mode is read as strict, so a damaged enforcement state never enforces less. (4) A session under a public root is pinned to public_root_sessions (D-22); strict mode judges its targets by that space's reads, not by 'public only'. (5) A path in no space (/tmp, /usr, /opt) is always allowed; per-space TMPDIRs (D-53, SP-046) are the boundary for temp files.

reconvene.topic: Wire the guard verdict into not-enforced records
reconvene.detail: SP-070.2.a2 records, while the guard is off or in log, the verdict the guard would have given ('would refuse (<rule>)' in the rule field). SP-040's Decide is not on main yet, so orchd's seam server.guardVerdict is nil and such records carry only decision 'not enforced' with an empty rule; the test drives the seam with a fake verdict. SP-040 or SP-041 must set server.guardVerdict from Decide(policy, pin, enforcement, event). The rule column holds the would-be verdict rather than a new column, to avoid a command-log schema change while SP-073 changes that store.

reconvene.topic: What the hooks switch does
reconvene.detail: D-40 made the tool hooks a switch. Implemented as a fifth layer 'hooks' (on/off) beside the four of SP-070.1.a1. orch settings refuse turning the Claude Code tool hooks on or off; orch install writes them whatever a settings toggle says and leaves them out only while the switch is off (or when the switches cannot be read, it writes them). Switching hooks off has orchd turn Claude Code's PreToolUse and CwdChanged orch-hook entries off through the settings service, and on again when switched back or when a timer reverts. Codex's hooks.json is not managed by orch settings, so the switch does not remove Codex's pre-tool-use hook; Codex events keep being logged. Confirm this, or ask for Codex coverage.

reconvene.topic: What counts as a layer being off
reconvene.detail: The digest and orch status name a layer when its switch is off, when the guard is in 'log' (it records but does not enforce), and when the hooks switch is on but Claude Code's tool hooks are turned off, missing or removed in settings.json (or cannot be checked). With a spaces policy applied, a tool hook with no settings row at all also counts, judged by whether orch's session-start hook is in Claude Code's settings. 'strict' is not named. With no policy applied, a never-installed tool hook is not named in the digest (orch status lists it under harness wiring), so orch behaves as before spaces. Confirm.

reconvene.topic: Layers that read the switches
reconvene.detail: Today only the guard switch changes behavior (command log records while off; the digest and status for all layers). Memory filtering (SP-025), outbound terms (SP-044, SP-045), generated sandbox rules (SP-046) and the enforcing guard (SP-041, which must fail closed in enforcing states per INV-13 and needs the enforcement state in the read-only file it reads) must read enforcement.state for their layer when they land. The app's switches and banner are SP-072.

reconvene.topic: SP-070 security review lows and accepted limits
reconvene.detail: From four security-audit rounds on PR #167 (all critical/high/medium fixed): (1) operator-only rests on refuseNonOperator, so a process an agent detaches from its session (reparented to launchd) passes as the operator, as for ApplySpaces; (2) a process running as the user can write spaces_enforcement and its log consistently while orchd is stopped, which the next start takes (the switch still shows in every digest and status); (3) a project-level Claude Code 'disableAllHooks' turns off every hook including the digest, outside any switch; (4) when orchd does not answer, the digest's fallback reads orch.db's switches but not whether the tool hooks are still in settings.json; (5) with every orch hook gone from Claude Code's settings no digest runs and the hooks layer reads as enforcing (orch status lists the tool hooks as missing); (6) markGuardState labels an event with the guard state when orchd stores it, a few milliseconds after the hook ran, and the log's writer waits on the switches' lock while a switch writes settings.json; (7) GetEnforcement is open to every caller and checks Claude Code's settings at most every 5 s; (8) settings.Service.List ignores a sync error except through the provider state, which the hooks check now reads. Self-protection paths (SP-042) and the OS sandbox (SP-046) are the answers to (1)-(3).

reconvene.topic: Timed switch limits
reconvene.detail: A timed switch lasts from 1 s to 24 h ('--for 15m'); an untimed switch has no limit and shows in every digest until switched back. A timed switch set over another keeps the first one's revert state, so a chain ends where it began; an untimed set replaces any timer. Confirm the 24 h cap, or choose another.

reconvene.topic: Flaky TestWatchTasksStreamsSnapshotChangesAndTicks
reconvene.detail: internal/daemon's TestWatchTasksStreamsSnapshotChangesAndTicks fails under load from parallel test runs ('WatchTasks ended with context canceled', taskwatch_test.go:117): about 4 of 16 full package runs on the SP-070 branch while three feature agents tested on this machine, 0 of 3 on main and 0 of 4 on the branch when the machine was quieter, 10 of 10 alone. The test and internal/daemon/taskwatch.go are untouched by SP-070. Likely cause: when the client cancels while WatchTasks is sending a tick or a change (the test's tick is 50 ms), the send returns the context error instead of WatchTasks returning nil. Fix in WatchTasks (return nil when ctx.Err() is set after a failed send) or add to the flaky list with RC-39.
reconvene.note: Resolved on 2026-11-11 by https://github.com/willesq/orchestrator/pull/168 (fixed on the user's instruction): WatchTasks now returns nil when a read or send fails after the client's context is done (a cancel during a snapshot, change or tick read, or select picking a ready tick or change over ctx.Done). TestWatchTasksEndsCleanlyWhenClientGoesAwayMidRead cancels at each read point and failed on every run before the fix.

reconvene.topic: Flaky tests after the parallel SP-040/SP-073/SP-070 merges
reconvene.detail: Seen on 2026-11-11 while merging main into SP-070 (coordinator session). (1) TestWatchTasksStreamsSnapshotChangesAndTicks (internal/daemon) fails 'WatchTasks ended with context canceled' in 2 of 2 package runs on main at faa84d2 (after SP-073) and in 3 of 4 runs on the SP-070 merge on this Mac, but passes 20/20 run alone and passed CI on Linux; more often than RC-66's 'about 1 in 5', so SP-073's task-anchor follower (it holds one task hub watcher slot, RC-67) may make it worse. See RC-66 and RC-92 for the cause and fix. (2) TestDecideCases (internal/spaces, SP-040) failed once under the full parallel suite: Targets hit its time budget ('analysis took too long'), so the case 'session pinned to no space reads a private space' got analysis_limit instead of within_space; it passes alone (3/3). The table test should give Targets a budget that load cannot exhaust, or retry on a limit reason.
reconvene.note: Part (1) fixed on 2026-11-11 by https://github.com/willesq/orchestrator/pull/168 (fixed on the user's instruction): WatchTasks ends cleanly when the client goes away mid-read; see RC-92. Part (2) remains open: TestDecideCases' 100 ms Targets budget can be exhausted under load.

reconvene.topic: Combine the outbound terms check with the enforcing guard at rebase
reconvene.detail: SP-044 runs its check in orch-hook pre-tool-use on its own (branched from main before SP-041, PR #172, merged): it prints its own deny and the command log does not record the refusal as a decision. When the two meet: one deny path, the terms refusal recorded in the command log as refused with rule outbound_term or outbound_unchecked, the hook tests' TestMain (SP-041) covering the terms tests, and the terms check reading the terms layer switch from SP-041's snapshot instead of orch.db. SP-042's ProtectedPaths already refuses reads of terms files.

reconvene.topic: What the outbound terms check does not see
reconvene.detail: Accepted for now and documented (docs/internals/hooks.md, Outbound terms): text sent by a script or program that runs git itself (./deploy.sh, make), an interpreter, curl to the GitHub API, or a tool other than a shell (notably GitHub MCP tools), and commits a push would send that a session hid by moving local remote-tracking refs. gh search and gh api GET queries send terms to GitHub without publishing them. Proposed: cover GitHub MCP tools' write calls the same way, and compare with git ls-remote before a push when a remote's tracking ref moved in the same session.
reconvene.note: 2026-11-14: settled by D-60 (best-effort, loosened baseline in SP-044; configurable rules in SP-075).

reconvene.topic: How strict the outbound terms check is
reconvene.detail: While the terms layer is on, SP-044 fails closed (outbound_unchecked) on any outbound command it cannot read in full: a variable or command substitution in it (except $HOME and $(cat <<'EOF' ...)), a command name built from a variable, loops, eval/xargs, git -c beyond a small allowlist, an earlier command that changes a remote or config, gh fed from a pipe. A gh write without -R counts every remote of the checkout (and GH_REPO) as a destination, so a fork whose upstream is another space's refuses the session's own terms in gh pr create. After git add/commit in the same call a push also checks the work tree, untracked files and every branch. Confirm this strictness, or say which cases should be allowed.
reconvene.note: 2026-11-14: settled by D-60 (best-effort, loosened baseline in SP-044; configurable rules in SP-075).

reconvene.topic: Outbound terms elsewhere than the command log (INV-07)
reconvene.detail: SP-044 keeps terms out of refusals, the command log, orchd's log and status output. Session transcripts, session records and anything indexed into RAG from them, the PR digests and event streams can still hold a term a session typed; INV-07 lists SP-053 for those. The terms cache in orchd notices a changed terms file by size and modification time only.

features.title: Record real hook payloads across harnesses
features.summary: A throwaway logging hook captures SessionStart, PreToolUse/BeforeTool, PostToolUse, CwdChanged and SessionEnd payloads for Claude Code and Codex across directory-change scenarios, and turns them into committed test fixtures.
features.why: The pin and guard depend on how each harness reports cwd. Only Claude Code's behavior is documented, and only in prose.

checkpoints.title: Capture tool

acceptance.check: A capture script installs a logging hook into a temporary harness home and writes each payload as one JSON line, with credentials redacted.
acceptance.measure: scenarios runnable without touching the real ~/.claude, ~/.codex or ~/.gemini

evidence: scripts/hook-capture.sh setup <dir> builds internal/hook/capture/cmd/hook-capture and installs the logging hook only into project-local settings of a scratch git project (<dir>/project/.claude/settings.local.json, <dir>/project/.codex/hooks.json; both git-excluded). Each event is one JSON line in <dir>/payloads/<harness>.jsonl, labelled by `scenario`; `summary` prints scenario/event/cwd/hook_cwd/tool per line; `clean` removes only directories carrying its marker.

Never touches the real harness homes: with HOME set to a fake home, setup refused <home>, <home>/.claude/cap, <home>/.codex/a, <home>/.config/orch/x, a symlink into <home>/.claude, and <missing>/../<home>/.claude/cap, all exit 1 with nothing created (2026-11-08). Codex runs with --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust so no hook trust is written to ~/.codex.

Credentials redacted: redaction runs on every decoded string value (internal/redact), plus scenario and hook_cwd. Tests in internal/hook/capture: TestCaptureAppendsOneLinePerEvent, TestCaptureRedactsSecrets, TestCaptureRedactsTokensAfterJSONEscapes, TestCapturePrivateKeyAcrossFieldsKeepsValidJSON, TestCaptureRedactsScenarioAndHookCwd, TestCaptureTruncatesLargeToolResponse, TestCaptureKeepsNonObjectInput, TestCaptureDeniesMarkedPreToolUse, TestCaptureDenyMarkerOnlyInToolInput, TestCaptureRejectsUnsafeHarnessName, TestCaptureReportsUnwritableDir: all pass; package coverage 91.2%; shellcheck clean.

security-audit of the capture tool on 2026-11-08: 0 critical/high; 2 medium (dot-dot path past the home guard; redaction on encoded JSON missing tokens after escapes) and lows L1-L6 fixed in this commit with the tests above.

checkpoints.title: Claude Code scenarios

acceptance.check: Record: plain cd within project; cd outside project; 'cd x && cmd' in one call; absolute path read; git -C; Read tool on an outside path; subagent in another directory; /cd; worktree enter; CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1 on and off; resume; compact.
acceptance.measure: scenarios recorded with observed cwd in PreToolUse, CwdChanged and the next PreToolUse

evidence: Recorded 2026-11-08 with scripts/hook-capture.sh, Claude Code 2.1.309, headless `claude -p` sessions in a scratch project (user approved headless runs on 2026-11-08). 13 scenarios with cwd observed in PreToolUse, CwdChanged and the next PreToolUse: C01 cd within, C02 cd outside, C03 cd x && cmd, C04 absolute path in Bash, C05 git -C, C06 Read tool outside, C07 subagent cd outside, C08 MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1, C09 =0, C10 resume, C11 compact, C12 EnterWorktree, C14 PreToolUse deny. C13 /cd: not available in headless mode ("/cd isn't available in this environment").

Findings: (1) cd within the project: CwdChanged(old_cwd,new_cwd) fires and the next PreToolUse cwd follows. (2) cd outside the project (C02, C03, C07) or any cd with MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1 (C08): CwdChanged fires with the new dir, then the shell is reset to the project with NO CwdChanged back; the next PreToolUse cwd is the project. CwdChanged's own cwd field was the new dir in C02 but the old dir in C07. (3) Absolute paths, git -C and Read file_path never change cwd; targets exist only in tool_input. (4) Subagent tool calls share the parent session_id and add agent_id/agent_type; a cd inside a subagent did not persist and fired no CwdChanged. (5) Resume restarts in the project root, not the last cwd (source=resume). (6) Compact: PreCompact(trigger=manual), SessionStart(source=compact), PostCompact; cwd unchanged. (7) EnterWorktree moves cwd into .claude/worktrees/<name> with NO CwdChanged. (8) PreToolUse deny (hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision=deny + reason) blocks the call; no PostToolUse follows and the model sees the reason. (9) Another PreToolUse hook (rtk) rewrote tool_input (ls -> rtk ls), visible only in PostToolUse: a guard must judge the input that actually runs.

checkpoints.title: Codex scenarios

acceptance.check: Same scenario list for Codex where supported; note which events exist and whether PreToolUse deny works.

evidence: Recorded 2026-11-08 with scripts/hook-capture.sh, codex-cli 0.166.0, headless `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` in the scratch project (user approved the batch on 2026-11-08). Codex ignores an untrusted project's .codex/hooks.json even with the trust bypass: the first run recorded nothing until the user trusted the scratch project interactively. 10 scenarios recorded: X01 cd within, X02 cd outside, X03 cd x && cmd, X04 absolute path in shell, X05 git -C, X06 shell workdir parameter outside, X07 PreToolUse deny, X08 apply_patch on an outside path, X09 resume, X11 subagent with workdir outside. X10 /compact via `codex exec resume` did not compact (no PreCompact; the text went to the model as a prompt).

Findings: (1) Codex has no CwdChanged event (0.166 events: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, SessionEnd, plus model/interrupt events). (2) Each shell call is independent: cd never persists and payload cwd stays the session root (X01-X03). (3) The shell tool's workdir parameter moves payload cwd (X06, X11: cwd=outside) while tool_input holds only `command` and the hook process still runs in the project; the guard must use payload cwd, not its own working directory. (4) Shell tool_name is `Bash`; file edits use tool_name `apply_patch` with the target path only inside tool_input.command (`*** Update File: <path>`) (X08). (5) Subagents: spawn/wait tools appear as `collaborationspawn_agent`/`collaborationwait_agent`; subagent tool calls keep the parent session_id and add agent_id/agent_type (X11). (6) Resume: SessionStart source=resume, cwd = session root (X09). (7) PreToolUse deny with hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision=deny plus a non-empty permissionDecisionReason blocks the call; no PostToolUse follows (X07). Codex rejects `ask`, a deny without a reason, and updatedInput without allow (binary strings).

features.title: Measure Qdrant costs of a collection per space
features.summary: Benchmark search latency across several collections fused with RRF versus one filtered collection, and measure set_payload relabel throughput.
features.why: R-03 changes the storage layout; the cost must be measured, not assumed.

checkpoints.title: Baseline

acceptance.check: Hybrid search p50/p95 on one collection of 40,000 synthetic chunks with a payload filter, 200 queries.

evidence: a1: TestIntegrationSpacesCost (internal/rag/spaces_bench_it_test.go; ORCH_QDRANT_BENCH=1, qdrant v1.17.1 native, Apple M3 Max 16 cores, 2026-11-08). One hybrid collection of 40,000 synthetic chunks (384-d dense clustered around 256 centres, BM25 from the real tokenizer over a Zipf vocabulary), searched through Service.Search (hybrid, weighted ranking, TopK 10) with payload filter tags any [space:s0 space:s1] (50% of chunks), 200 queries after 20 warm-up. Default segments (auto): p50 16.45 ms, p95 17.06 ms. With ORCH_QDRANT_BENCH_SEGMENTS=2: p50 11.22 ms, p95 11.77 ms. Recorded.

checkpoints.title: Multi-collection

acceptance.check: Same corpus split across 4 collections; search the 2 allowed collections and fuse.
acceptance.threshold: <= 1.3x baseline, else document and revisit R-03

acceptance.check: Relabel by set_payload with a filter over 40,000 chunks.

evidence: a1: TestIntegrationSpacesCost, same corpus split across 4 collections; the 2 allowed collections searched in parallel through Service.Search (each with its own space tag filter as the second layer) and fused by RRF (k=60), 200 queries interleaved with the baseline. Default segments: p50 30.75-31.13 ms, p95 32.64-32.94 ms, ratio 1.93-1.94x over 3 runs. ORCH_QDRANT_BENCH_SEGMENTS=2: p50 16.45 ms, p95 17.54 ms, ratio 1.49x. Over the 1.3x threshold, so documented in docs/internals/memory.md ('Cost of a collection per space'): request latency barely depends on collection size; the keyword request returning dense vectors costs 8.2-9.0 ms (1.8-2.0 ms without them); the engine did not overlap concurrent requests (4 parallel raw requests 13-30 ms), so each extra collection adds a whole hybrid search. Top-10 agreement between layouts 85.5%. R-03 (now D-10) to be revisited with the user.

a2: TestIntegrationSpacesCost, POST /points/payload?wait=true with a filter matching all 40,000 chunks: one collection 0.33 s (default segments; 10.3 s with 2 segments); 4 space collections, one filtered set_payload each, 0.39-0.44 s total. Count afterwards = 40,000 relabelled. Threshold <= 120 s met.

a1 revisit: R-03 (D-10) revisited with the user on 2026-11-08 after this measurement; decision: keep a collection per space and accept the measured cost (recorded as D-24). Confirmed by user on 2026-11-08.

features.title: Verify how harness sandbox and permission settings layer
features.summary: Determine which settings files apply to a session started in a subfolder, whether per-space CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR profiles work (including whether they need a separate login), and what the Codex sandbox can deny.
features.why: Layers 3 and 4 (OS sandbox deny, file-tool deny rules) need per-space settings.

checkpoints.title: Claude Code

acceptance.check: With a temp home: a sandbox denyRead on a folder blocks 'cat' into it; a Read(...) permission deny blocks the Read tool; record which of user, project and local settings apply when launched from a subfolder.

evidence: Recorded 2026-11-08, Claude Code 2.1.309, 16 headless `claude -p --model haiku` sessions in scratch git repos under the session scratchpad (user approved 11 + 5 runs on 2026-11-08). The user chose 'use my real config read-only' over logging in to a temp profile, so the user layer is the unmodified ~/.claude/settings.json; its env key DISABLE_TELEMETRY served as the user-layer marker. Every other layer set a distinct env marker read back with `env | grep`.

Layering matrix: L2 from checkout root -> user, project settings.json, local settings.local.json. L3 from repo/sub with its own .claude/ -> user, ROOT local, sub project, sub local; root project NOT applied. L4 from repo/sub/deep (no .claude) -> user, ROOT local only; root project NOT applied. L6 (fresh repo2/sub/deep) confirms L4: user + root local only. L5 from a non-git child of a dir with .claude/ -> user only.

Sandbox: S1 (root of sbx1; project sandbox.enabled=true, allowUnsandboxedCommands=false, filesystem.denyRead=[jobB]; local denyRead=[jobC]) -> `cat` of both fails 'Operation not permitted', so project and local denyRead merge and project enabled=true overrides user enabled=false. S1c same repo -> Read tool RETURNED jobB's file: sandbox denyRead does not block the Read tool. S1b2 (sbx1/sub, --permission-mode default) -> both files printed, consistent with root project settings not applying from a subfolder.

Read deny: S2 (project deny Read(//<abs jobC>/**), sandbox on) -> Read tool error 'File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings'. S2b2 same repo, Bash `cat` -> 'Operation not permitted': a Read deny also feeds the sandbox's denied reads. S2c from sbx2/sub -> file read (project settings not applied). S3 single-slash Read(/<abs>/**) -> not blocked (resolved relative to the settings file). S4/S4b (deny in ROOT settings.local.json) -> Read blocked from the root and from a subfolder.

Separate login: L0 fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and L1 temp HOME both exit 1 with 'Not logged in · Please run /login', so a per-space CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR profile needs its own login; persistence of that login per profile was not tested (the user declined the temp-profile login). S1b/S2b first runs were refused by the user's auto-mode classifier before reaching the sandbox (inconclusive), rerun as S1b2/S2b2 with --permission-mode default.
Matrix and conclusions recorded in docs/internals/install.md 'Harness sandbox and permission layering'.

features.title: Spaces config, validation, apply and drift
features.summary: orch.db holds the spaces policy as numbered revisions (JSON document and sha256): drafts and the applied one. The policy has kinds public/isolated/private and bindings (github_orgs, roots, web_prefixes, chat, reads, terms_file). Roots may nest when the inner root is at least as strict (D-15). orchd validates, keeps enforcing the last good applied revision, and reports drift when a draft is pending or the applied row no longer matches its hash. SetSpacesDraft, DiffSpaces and ApplySpaces RPCs; apply is operator-only and names the reviewed revision.
