acceptance.check: Each rule rejects with a specific error: an org, prefix or tenant bound twice; the same root bound twice; a nested root less strict than a root above it (strictness public < private < isolated); a root of one isolated space nested in another isolated space; isolated reads another isolated space; private reads isolated; public reads anything else; terms file inside a git tree; unknown kind.
An invalid config never replaces the applied one; the error is reported in status.
The nested-root fixture (~/code public, ~/code/willesq private, ~/code/company1 isolated) is accepted.
An isolated space listing a private space in reads is accepted; without the entry it cannot read it.

public_root_sessions names the space for session content from sessions pinned under a public root; it must be a private or isolated space; default is the only private space if exactly one exists, else quarantine.

features.title: Placement classifier and 'why'
features.summary: Classify(origin, policy) -> space | quarantine | conflict, as a pure function over the origin schema. Roots resolve CODEOWNERS-style: the deepest matching root decides. When root and git remote disagree, the stricter wins; two different isolated spaces are a conflict. A sticky retag override for a source_uri wins over rules. ExplainPlacement RPC and 'orch spaces why' show every matching root from shallowest to deepest, the remote's effect and the result.
features.why: INV-03; one place decides placement for every writer and for the UI tester.

checkpoints.title: Cases

acceptance.check: Table test covers: repo in isolated org; fork owned by a job org with a public parent; public repo in public org; private repo in public org; repo transferred between orgs; root and remote agree; remote stricter than root (remote wins); root stricter than remote (root wins); root and remote in two isolated spaces (conflict); nested roots: path under ~/code (public), ~/code/willesq (private), ~/code/company1 (isolated) and a deeper path under each; remote only, no root; no root and no remote; allowlisted web prefix; web page ingested by a session (session's space); Slack and Teams tenants; client ingest from a pinned session; sticky retag override; unmatched.
Unmatched and conflicting origins never return public.
A session pinned under a public root reads public only, and its writes are placed in public_root_sessions (D-22).

evidence: a1: TestClassifyCases (internal/spaces/classify_test.go) has 57 table cases, all passing. It covers every listed case: repo in isolated org; fork owned by a job org with a public parent; public repo in public org; private repo in public org; repo transferred between orgs (public->job: remote_stricter; job->job: conflict); root and remote agree; remote stricter; root stricter; two isolated spaces (conflict); nested roots ~/code (public), ~/code/willesq (private), ~/code/company1 (isolated) and a deeper path under each, plus case-folding and the sibling-prefix boundary; remote only, no root; no root and no remote; allowlisted web prefix; web page ingested by a session (D-14); Slack and Teams tenants; client ingest from a pinned session; sticky retag override (incl. over a conflict, to quarantine, to a removed space); unmatched. Also TestClassifyRemoteEffect, TestClassifyWithoutPolicy (INV-10: no policy -> shared), TestEnginePlace (org binding confirmed/suspended from orch.db), TestPrefixKeyNormalizes and TestWebPrefixBoundaries.

a2: TestClassifyNeverPublicWhenUnplaced runs a property test over 20,000 seeded random origins across every system, path, remote owner/visibility, URL, writer, tenant and org-confirmation state. No unmatched, conflicting or quarantined origin returns a public space; all of them return quarantine. Session content is never placed in public. Passes, and passes 20 times under -race.

a3: TestSessionUnderPublicRoot checks D-22. A session pinned under the public root ~/code reads as 'oss', and res.CanRead(ReadAs, x) is true only for public spaces (not personal, acme, globex or quarantine). Its content goes to public_root_sessions (personal, rule public_root_session). With no default space and two private spaces, the content goes to quarantine and the session still reads public only. Passes.

checkpoints.title: Explain

acceptance.check: 'orch spaces why <path|url|org/repo|chat-uri>' prints every matching root from shallowest to deepest, the remote's effect, the deciding rule and the result for each case above; agents may call it only for targets resolving to their own space or public.

evidence: a1: TestExplainPlacementCases (internal/daemon/placement_rpc_test.go) drives the ExplainPlacement RPC over temporary git checkouts with a fake gh. It covers 19 targetable cases: path, owner/repo, URL and slack:/teams: chat URIs, including the slack:// form. Every case asserts: every matching root shallowest to deepest, the remote's owner/repo/visibility/space/effect, the deciding rule and reason, the result, and for paths the session's write space and read-as space. Writer, client and override cases cannot be named as a 'why' target and are covered by TestClassifyCases. TestSpacesWhy (internal/cli/spaces_cmd_test.go) checks that 'orch spaces why' prints roots shallowest first with the deepest marked, the remote's effect, 'rule: <rule>: <reason>', 'result: <space> (<outcome>)' and the session line, and that it makes ~ and ./ paths absolute.

features.title: Session liveness and session list
features.summary: orchd decides whether each pinned session is still running from the kernel, not from hook events: the pin's harness PID must exist with the same process start time. States: active (process alive, a hook event in the last 30 min), idle (process alive, no event for 30 min or more; a session left open for a week stays idle, not ended), ended (SessionEnd received, or the process is gone, or the PID now belongs to a different process; ended_at is the time orchd noticed), unpinned (a running claude, codex or gemini process with no pin, e.g. started before the hooks were installed). A sweep runs every 60 s. 'orch sessions list [--all]' and a ListSessions RPC show harness, session id, PID, space, pinned directory, state, last activity, tool-event count and refusals. A resumed session (SessionStart source=resume in a new process) rebinds the pin to the new PID and start time but never changes its space.
features.why: Sessions are often left open without /exit for days. Log retention and pins must follow the real process, not the last message.

features.title: Log retention sweeper
features.summary: orchd deletes a session's events N days after it ended (N = 3, 7 or 30; default 7), where 'ended' comes from SP-017: SessionEnd, or the process gone. A session whose process is still alive is never treated as ended, however long it has been idle; instead its log is capped at 50 MB, oldest non-refusal records first. Refusal records are kept 90 days. A total size cap (default 500 MB) deletes the oldest ended sessions first.
features.why: D-05. The log must not grow without bound.

Sweeping twice changes nothing the second time; chain heads of deleted sessions are kept.

features.title: Enforcement switches

Stored in orchd with the applied policy, set through SetEnforcement and 'orch spaces enforce <layer> <state> [--for 15m|1h]'. A timed switch reverts by itself. Every change emits an event. While any layer is off, orch status and every session's start digest say so. Logging never stops.

features.title: Enforcing guard in orch-hook (fail closed)
features.summary: pre-tool-use decides locally from two read-only files orchd writes (applied policy plus enforcement state, session pin) and emits each harness's deny format. This is a documented exception to the hook never-block contract: while the guard is in an enforcing state, a timeout or unreadable input means refuse. The refusal message names the rule and never the matched text.
features.why: D-11 (enforced from the first release), INV-13.

acceptance.check: Deny output matches each harness's documented format (Claude Code permissionDecision; Codex per SP-001).
Timeout, missing pin and unreadable policy each refuse in enforcing states, and allow when the guard is off or in log state.
Decision latency including file reads.

With the session's queue share full (flooded with ordinary events), a call the guard refuses is still stored in the command log with its decision; ordinary events past the share drop with a gap record (D-37).

orchd identifies each connection's peer by a kernel token (LOCAL_PEERTOKEN on macOS, SO_PEERPIDFD on Linux): a peer that hands its socket to a child and exits, with its PID then reused by a harness in another space, is not resolved to that harness's session; a peer that cannot be identified gets no space (D-44).
Replay of the SP-001 fixtures under block-other-jobs.
acceptance.measure: refusals for targets within the session's own space

acceptance.check: Switching the guard off through SP-070 takes effect for the next tool call of a running session.

features.title: Self-protection paths
features.summary: The guard refuses agent writes to orch's config and data directories, the policy snapshot and pin files, terms files, ~/.claude/settings*, ~/.codex/hooks.json and config, Gemini settings, and .git/hooks. This covers file tools and shell redirection targets.
features.why: Otherwise an agent could remove orch's hooks or edit the pin. Pattern from OpenAPPA's file-tracker.

acceptance.check: Write, Edit and MultiEdit, plus Bash '>', '>>', tee, sed -i, cp and mv into each protected path, are refused.
Reads of protected paths other than terms files and credentials remain allowed.

features.title: Live GitHub guard
features.summary: gh and git commands whose target repo or org belongs to another isolated space are refused: gh api repos/..., gh -R, gh repo clone, and git clone/fetch/push to such remotes.
features.why: An agent with one gh login could read the other employer's org directly, bypassing memory entirely.

acceptance.check: Covered command forms are refused for another job's org and allowed for the session's own space and public.

features.title: Per-job GitHub account follow-ups
features.summary: Follow-ups to SP-063 decided on 2026-11-10 (D-54): scopes and PR watching for orgs reachable only through a space's profile; GitHub calls a space's profile cannot read are refused, with stricter gh_config_dir checks; the repo picker and PR-outcome tracker use the space's profile; a GitHub API quota cap per isolated account.

acceptance.check: An org reachable only through a space's gh profile can be added to GitHub scopes and its PRs are watched and reviewed through that profile, never the default login.

A GitHub call made for a space through a profile that cannot read the target (repo or org outside the profile's access) is refused with a clear error, never retried with another login; gh_config_dir must be an absolute, owner-only directory under the user's home or the call is refused.
The repo picker and the PR-outcome tracker use the space's profile for that space's repos; a test shows the default login is not used for an isolated space's repo.
Each isolated account has a configurable GitHub API budget per hour; past it orchd defers that account's sync and watch calls (logged), while other accounts are unaffected.

features.title: Policy replay
features.summary: 'orch spaces replay <session|fixtures> [--policy <rev|file>]' re-decides recorded events and reports verdict changes. CI runs it over the SP-001 fixtures.
features.why: Policy changes are tested against real behavior before they apply (OpenAPPA replay pattern).

acceptance.check: Replay under the recording policy reproduces every recorded decision.
Replay under a changed policy lists each changed verdict with its rule id.

features.title: Minimal Spaces controls in the app
features.summary: Before the full Spaces pane: a Spaces section in the existing Settings pane (and the menu bar panel) with the enforcement switches and their timers, a banner while any layer is off, and a directory validator: type or pick a path and see every matching root from shallowest to deepest, the effective space, any git-remote adjustment, and why.
features.why: D-11 (switches in the UI from day one) and D-15 (directory validator).

acceptance.check: Each layer can be switched from the app; the change appears in orch status within 2 s; a timed switch shows its countdown.
Light and dark snapshots of the section and of the 'enforcement off' banner.

For the nested-root fixture (~/code public, ~/code/willesq private, ~/code/company1 isolated), the validator's chain and result equal ExplainPlacement for at least 8 paths, including a path under no root and a checkout whose remote is stricter than its root.

features.title: Stamp origin and space on every write
features.summary: All six IngestText writers record origin fields and run the classifier; the chunk payload gets origin.*, space and labels_v. Clients cannot set space; a client Ingest is placed in the caller's pinned space.
features.why: INV-02, INV-03; D-02 (docs follow the separation).

acceptance.check: One test per writer asserts origin, space and labels_v on stored chunks.
docs sync records repo visibility (add Private to docs.Repo) and owner node ID per repo.
A client-supplied 'space' or tag claiming a space is ignored; the chunk lands in the caller's pinned space or quarantine.

Docs sync, sources, the review watcher and PR monitoring each re-check the GitHub org binding (CheckOrg) before writing content; a sync of several repos re-checks between repos, and content from an org whose identity changed is not written (D-52).

features.title: A Qdrant collection per space
features.summary: Each space maps to its own collection (plus public and quarantine). Writes route by space; searches query only the caller's readable collections and fuse with RRF. Migration, reindex, backup and hybrid tooling work per collection. Every content or embedding cache is keyed by space.
features.why: R-03, INV-11; physical separation removes 'forgot the filter' bugs and cross-space BM25/IDF statistics.

acceptance.check: A recording fake store proves writes for space S touch only S's collection.
A recording fake store proves a search queries only the allowed collections.
The payload filter on space is still applied inside each collection (second layer).
MigrateHybrid, ReindexKeywords and DropBackup iterate every space collection.
Each cache key includes the space; a hit cached for space A is never served to space B.
Search p95 against the SP-002 baseline at 40,000 chunks.

features.title: Enforce spaces on every memory read path
features.summary: Search, GetDocument, ListSources, ListDocs, rag_list_sources, session recall, auto-RAG and 'rag why' resolve the caller's readable spaces (SP-011) and apply them inside orchd. Caller filters are combined with AND. A registry lists every read RPC with its space decision.
features.why: INV-01, INV-02.

acceptance.check: Two isolated spaces plus public, 200 chunks each. From a session in space A, every read path, queried with verbatim text of B's chunks, returns 0 hits, URIs or titles from B.
acceptance.measure: cross-space results across all read paths

acceptance.check: Public chunks are returned to sessions in every space and to sessions with no space.
A caller filter (tags, source_uri, scope) can narrow but never add a space.
With memory filtering switched off (SP-070), cross-space results are returned and every such response is logged as 'not enforced'.
A job session reads personal only when its space opted in (D-16); it never reads another job's space either way.

A session pinned through a harness started outside its session's process tree (a detached fake 'claude' pinned in another space's directory) reads no memory beyond what its original session may read; the SP-041 guard refusing that start is the precondition and is exercised in the test (D-38).

A caller resolved as the operator with no controlling terminal and not Orch.app (a process that double-forked or used launchctl/open/osascript out of a session) reads public memory only; the operator at a terminal and Orch.app keep operator-scope reads (D-39).

A queued task reads only what the session that dispatched it may read (its pin's space, public, and private spaces that space lists) and writes to that space; a task the operator dispatched uses the placement of its working directory; a task orchd does not track reads public only (D-46).
A test fails when an RPC that returns stored content has no entry in the space-decision registry (like taskCallable).

features.title: Close non-memory bleed paths
features.summary: Events, the SessionStart digest, per-prompt updates, ListPRs, ListGitHubItems, GetPRDetail, ListTasks, GetTask and PR reviews carry a space set at creation and are filtered for agent callers. The operator still sees everything, labelled.
features.why: INV-01. The session-start PR digest currently lists PRs from every org.

acceptance.check: One test per path: a session in space A sees no item from space B.
A cached PR's space comes from its repo owner, and a review task runs pinned to that space.

features.title: Relabel and migrate existing content
features.summary: 'orch rag relabel [--dry-run]' moves stale chunks (labels_v not current) into the right collection using stored origin, source_uri, checkout tags and the session table. Unplaceable chunks go to quarantine. Resumable. Dry-run prints counts per transition, never content.
features.why: INV-08, INV-03; stale labels are the documented failure in other systems (Onyx #15990).

acceptance.check: Stale chunks are unreadable before relabel and readable in the right space after.
A second run changes 0 chunks.
An interrupted run resumes without duplicating or losing chunks (count before = count after).
Dry-run output contains only counts and space names.
Relabel of 40,000 chunks.

features.title: Retag a source (move its data)
features.summary: RetagSource RPC (operator-only), 'orch spaces retag <source_uri> <space>' and the UI. orchd copies the source's points, vectors and payloads to the target space's collection, verifies the count, then deletes them from the old collection. No re-embedding. It records a sticky override (source_uri -> space) that later refreshes and re-ingests honor. Retagging into public, or out of an isolated space, needs explicit confirmation. Resumable.
features.why: D-14: the user stays in control of placement, and data is moved rather than duplicated.

acceptance.check: After a retag, the source's chunk count in the new collection equals the count before, the old collection holds 0 of its chunks, and the total chunk count is unchanged.
The fake embedder records no calls during a retag.
Search from the new space finds the source; search from the old space does not.
A retag interrupted after the copy and before the delete resumes to a single copy, with no duplicates and nothing lost.
A later docs sync, sources refresh or client re-ingest of the same source_uri lands in the retagged space.
Retag is refused for agent callers; retag into public or out of an isolated space without confirm is refused.
Moving a 2,000-chunk source.

features.title: Quarantine management
features.summary: 'orch quarantine list|assign|purge' (operator-only), with counts in orch status.
features.why: INV-03 needs a way out of quarantine that only the operator controls.

acceptance.check: list shows sources and counts; assign moves a source to a space and records an override rule; purge is dry-run by default and needs confirm.
All three are refused for agent callers.

features.title: Derived content and taint
features.summary: Summaries are made from one session at a time and inherit its space. Task records carry the dispatching session's space, and tasks run pinned to it. Files a session writes outside any root are recorded with the session's space, and a later ingest of them uses it. The operator's explicit cross-space reads taint that session.
features.why: INV-09; Copilot-style label inheritance; OpenAPPA file-tracker pattern.

acceptance.check: The summarizer never receives text from two sessions in one call; its output lands in that session's space.
A task dispatched from space A is pinned to A, searches as A and its events are in A.
A file written by an A session in /tmp and later ingested is placed in A.

features.title: Public-space write gate
features.summary: Only verified-public content reaches the public space automatically: repos GitHub reports as not private in a public-bound org, allowlisted web prefixes from sources refresh, and files under a root the operator declared public. Session writers never target public; a page a session ingests takes the session's space (D-14). Visibility is re-checked on every sync; a repo that turned private leaves public before anything else is indexed. Only an operator retag (SP-071) can move other content into public.
features.why: The public space is read by every session, so it carries the highest bar.

acceptance.check: A private repo in a public org goes to quarantine (or the configured space).
A public-to-private flip moves the repo's chunks out of public in the same sync, before other repos are indexed.
Unreadable visibility is treated as private.
Session, summary, hand-off and client writers can never target public.

Under a public root, content from a checkout whose remote is not GitHub, or that has no remote, is quarantined, not placed public; it becomes public only when the operator retags it or declares that folder public (D-50).

features.title: Visibility in status and 'rag why'
features.summary: orch status shows spaces, chunks per space, quarantine count, conflicts, drift and relabel progress. 'orch rag why' shows the caller's space and the collections searched.
features.why: Users and agents need to see the boundary to trust it.

acceptance.check: Status output includes the six fields; agent callers see counts only for their own space and public.

features.title: Outbound terms per space
features.summary: Each space may have a terms file (term or re:<regex> per line, case-insensitive, word boundaries), refused if inside a git tree. An outbound action is refused when its text contains a term from a space its destination (the target repo's owner) does not hold. Covers git commit message and staged diff, git push range, git tag -m, gh pr and issue create/edit/comment/review, gh api writes. Refusals give the term's line number and hash, never the term.
features.why: INV-07; the destination-based rule from the design.

checkpoints.title: Matching

acceptance.check: Parser and matcher table tests, including regex terms, case, word boundaries and invalid regex rejection.
A term in a staged file (not the message) is caught for git commit; a term in a pushed commit is caught for git push.

evidence: a1: TestTermsMatching (internal/spaces/terms_test.go): one terms file with literal terms (one word, two words, with punctuation, non-ASCII, a dotted host) and regex terms (a ticket pattern, an alternation), 26 match/no-match cases, all pass: case-insensitive, word boundaries (not inside falconry, refalcon, falcon_x, Überwaldx), regex anchoring by boundaries (INV-123 and INV-12345 do not match INV-[0-9]{4}), comments and blank lines skipped, CRLF lines. TestTermsRejected: 8 invalid files rejected (invalid regex, invalid character class, empty pattern, a pattern matching empty text, a line over 512 bytes, not UTF-8, over 256 KiB, over 4,096 terms), and no error text names the term; the error names the line. TestTermsRedact (5 cases incl. back-to-back terms and a regex with its own groups), TestRedactJSONAndTargets (reserved group names rejected), TestSpaceTerms, TestReadApplied.

a2: TestOutboundStagedTermCaught (internal/spaces/outbound_test.go, a real git repository whose origin is github.com/acme/app): a globex term in a staged file, with an innocent message, is refused for git commit (outbound_term, globex, line 1, destination acme), and so are commit -a with an unstaged tracked change, a term in the message and in a -F file; acme's own term to acme is allowed. TestOutboundPushedTermCaught: a globex term in a local commit not on origin is refused for git push, git push origin main, HEAD:main and -u origin --all; once origin's tracking ref has it the push is allowed; acme's term pushed to a globex URL is refused. Further: TestOutboundDestinations, TestOutboundFailsClosed, TestOutboundActions, and the three security reviews' reproducers TestOutboundReviewCases, TestOutboundReview2Cases, TestOutboundReview3Cases and TestOutboundNoFilterRun (a repository's clean filter does not run).

checkpoints.title: Never leaked

acceptance.check: A test greps refusal text, the command log, orchd logs and status output for each fixture term.

evidence: a1: TestTermsNeverLeak (internal/daemon/terms_redact_test.go): with two jobs' terms files (literal and regex terms) applied, 16 tool events carrying every fixture term in commands, paths, directories (cwd, old and new cwd) and a Write tool's content (after newline and tab escapes, and past the 2 KB command cap) are stored; the command log records, orchd's log output during the run, the Status RPC output and a refusal reason for each term hold 0 occurrences of any fixture term (commands read [term]). TestTermsWithheldWhenUnreadable: with a terms file gone, command, targets and directories are withheld. The hook's refusal text is checked too: TestOutboundTermsRefusedByHook (internal/hook/terms_test.go) prints the PreToolUse deny naming the rule and the term's space, and not the term.

features.blocked_reason: Needs a user decision on residual risk (DOD-6 cannot reach zero open findings by more fixing). Three security-audit rounds of the outbound terms check each found new ways around static shell reading (round 3: 4 high, 7 medium, all fixed in this branch with regression tests; a fourth round would likely find more, as D-28 recorded for target extraction). Proposed decision, like D-28: SP-044's hook check is best-effort; SP-045's git hooks (commit-msg, pre-push on real content) and per-job GitHub accounts (D-18) are the boundary for git, and the residual classes (zsh and profile aliases/functions, scripts and programs that run git, interpreters, curl, non-shell tools, forged tracking refs) are accepted risk recorded in RC-117/RC-118. Confirm, or say what more SP-044 must cover. All acceptance items pass locally; the independent verifier and CI were not run because of this block.

features.title: Git hook helper for terms
features.summary: 'orch guard git-hook --install' adds commit-msg and pre-push hooks to a repo (or core.hooksPath) that run the same term check for any committer, including the user's own terminal.
features.why: The agent hook cannot see commits made outside agent sessions or obfuscated commands.

acceptance.check: Install is dry-run by default, idempotent, backs up and chains existing hooks rather than replacing them, and uninstalls cleanly.
A commit containing a term is refused; one without passes; an existing hook still runs.

features.title: Per-space harness settings: per-checkout files and launcher
features.summary: Two delivery paths (D-23). (1) Automatic: orch keeps .claude/settings.local.json in every checkout under a space's roots, holding sandbox.filesystem.denyRead/denyWrite and Read(...)/Edit(...) denies for other isolated spaces' roots plus env GH_CONFIG_DIR for the space's gh profile. It merges with the user's own local settings, re-syncs when roots, checkouts or the policy change, and makes sure the file is ignored by git (adding it to .git/info/exclude when no ignore rule covers it). (2) Optional: 'orch run <space> -- claude|codex' starts a session with a generated per-space profile (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and Codex's equivalent if SP-004 finds one), so it works from any folder. Both are switchable through SP-070's sandbox layer.
features.why: The OS sandbox is the only layer that holds against commands that build paths at runtime; GH_CONFIG_DIR gives agent shells the job's own GitHub account (D-18).

acceptance.check: Generated settings for a checkout in space A deny every other isolated root, deny nothing in A, public or opted-in private spaces, and set GH_CONFIG_DIR to A's profile.
Existing user entries in settings.local.json are preserved; repeat generation is idempotent; a backup is kept before the first change.
After generation, 'git check-ignore' reports the file ignored in every checkout; orch adds a .git/info/exclude entry only when no rule covers it and never edits a tracked .gitignore.
A new clone under a space root gets its settings file.
In a temp home, a sandboxed 'cat' of a file in another job's root fails, and 'gh auth status' in the agent shell shows the space's account.

'orch run <space>' and the per-checkout settings give each space its own TMPDIR and deny other spaces' temp directories; a session in one space cannot read a file another space's session wrote under its TMPDIR (D-53).

With sandbox.enabled, allowUnsandboxedCommands=false and the Read(//...) denies written together in a checkout's root settings.local.json, a Claude Code session started in a subfolder is refused Read, Grep, Glob and Edit on another space's root (D-53).

'orch run <space> -- claude' sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (and GH_CONFIG_DIR) for the child process only, and refuses an unknown space or a space the current folder resolves outside of unless --force is given.
A session started with the launcher from ~/scratch gets the same deny rules as one started inside a checkout of that space.
Whether a separate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR needs its own Claude login is documented from SP-004, with the setup steps.
Switching the sandbox layer off (SP-070) removes orch's entries from every generated file and leaves user entries intact; switching it on restores them.

features.title: Refusal events and notifications
features.summary: Each refusal emits an event (session, space, tool, rule, term line number or hash, no content) to the operator's stream and the app's Needs-you section.
features.why: Refusals should be visible without reading logs.

acceptance.check: An event is emitted for each refusal with the required fields and no command text.

features.title: RPCs for the Spaces pane
features.summary: ListSpaces, ScanSpaces (read-only scan of chosen folders for git remotes, plus gh org membership and repo visibility), ExplainPlacement, ListSessionPins, ListToolEvents, DiffSpaces, ApplySpaces (operator-only, revision-checked).
features.why: The app is a thin client; orchd owns the logic.

acceptance.check: Each RPC has handler tests; taskCallable and operatorActions are updated, and a test asserts ApplySpaces is operator-only.

plan_location.note: Status on origin/main is authoritative. A feature's status changes on its feature branch and reaches main when its PR merges.

progress_file.purpose: Live progress for the user and the next session. The plan's status only changes on main when a PR merges; this file shows what is happening now. It is never committed (listed in .git/info/exclude).

schema.updated_at: UTC ISO 8601, set on every write
schema.step: the session_procedure step being executed, e.g. '6. checkpoints'
schema.checkpoint: id of the checkpoint being worked on, or null
schema.checkpoints_done: ids of this feature's checkpoints with evidence
schema.note: one plain sentence for the user: what is happening or what you need from them
schema.history: list of {at, feature, event}, newest last, keep the last 50; append, never rewrite earlier entries

status_values.in_progress: a session has started it on its feature branch
status_values.blocked: cannot continue without the user; blocked_reason says why
status_values.done: every acceptance item met and independently verified; passes=true, verified_sha and verified_at set
status_values.superseded: retired by an explicit user decision; kept for history, never deleted

session_procedure: 1. Sync. In the main checkout (/Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator) run `git fetch origin`. Read the plan from origin/main: `git show origin/main:docs/spaces/spaces-features.json`. That copy is authoritative for status; local copies may be stale.

2. Pick exactly one feature: the first feature in ascending 'priority' whose status on origin/main is not 'done' or 'superseded'. Never skip it, never choose another, never work on two at once. Run one session at a time.

3. Look for existing work on it. First read the live progress file (/Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator/docs/spaces/progress.local.json): if it names a different session_id with status 'in_progress' and updated_at less than 30 minutes ago, another session is working. Stop and tell the user. Then check branches and PRs: the branch is feat/<id in lowercase>-<short-slug> (e.g. feat/sp-020-spaces-config); run `git branch -a --list '*feat/<id>-*'` and `gh pr list --state all --search '<ID> in:title'`.

3a. If an open PR exists whose plan copy already shows the feature 'done' with verification, it is waiting for the user to review and merge. Report the PR link and stop. Do not start the next feature.

3b. If a branch or open PR exists but the feature isn't done there, resume it: use its existing worktree under /Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator.worktrees/feat/..., or recreate it with ~/.claude/orchestrator/scripts/git_worktree_create.sh <branch> and answer 'y' to reuse the existing branch.
3c. If the PR was merged but origin/main doesn't show the feature done, or a PR was closed unmerged, stop and ask the user what happened.
3d. If nothing exists, run ~/.claude/orchestrator/scripts/git_worktree_create.sh feat/<id>-<slug> from the main checkout and work only in that worktree.

4. Preconditions. Every depends_on feature must be 'done' on origin/main, and no entry in decisions.open may list this feature in 'blocks'. If either fails, stop and tell the user. (Priority order makes the first case unexpected.)

5. On the feature branch, set the feature's status to 'in_progress', increment 'attempts', and set 'branch'. Commit (signed). Push, open a draft PR titled 'feat(spaces): <summary> (<ID>)' early, record its URL in the feature's 'pr' field, and register it in ~/.pr-watch.json. Write the live progress file now and after every later step, checkpoint, block or finish (schema in plan_location.progress_file); make sure docs/spaces/progress.local.json is listed in the main checkout's .git/info/exclude.

6. Do the checkpoints in order. After each one, record evidence (test names, command output, measured numbers, or 'confirmed by user on <date>' for manual items) in that checkpoint's 'evidence' array and commit. Update the live progress file (checkpoint, checkpoints_done, note, a history entry) at the start and end of each checkpoint.

7. Manual items need the user: ask them to perform or confirm the step and wait. If you can't continue for any reason (missing input, a criterion that is wrong or impossible, 3 failed fix rounds), set status 'blocked' with a specific blocked_reason, commit, push, and stop. Never move past a blocked feature. When you stop or need the user, the live file's status and note must say so.

8. When every checkpoint has evidence meeting its threshold, run every definition_of_done check yourself. Then spawn an independent verifier: a fresh subagent that gets only the diff (origin/main...HEAD), this feature's JSON, the invariants it appears in, and definition_of_done. It re-runs every test, command and metric itself and reports pass or fail for each acceptance item and each DOD check. It does not see your reasoning.

9. If the verifier reports any failure, fix it and verify again, up to 3 rounds; after that, set 'blocked'. If everything passes, set status 'done', passes=true, verified_sha to the commit that was verified, verified_at to the current UTC time (ISO 8601). Commit that change (signed) and push. Leave the PR as a draft; the user marks it ready and merges.

10. Never delete, renumber or reorder features, checkpoints or acceptance items, and never edit acceptance criteria (criteria_sha256 detects it). Only the user may mark a feature 'superseded'. If you discover new work, describe it under 'Proposed new features' in the PR body; it is appended to the plan, with the next free ID, only after the user approves.

11. Finish with a short report: the feature, its PR link, the verification result, what is waiting on the user, and which feature step 2 will pick next once this one is merged. Leave the live progress file with the final status ('done', 'blocked' or 'idle') and a note matching your report.

12. Record decisions as you go, until the last feature is done. A decision the user makes goes to decisions.confirmed_by_user with the next D-id and the date. Everything else that needs the user later goes to decisions.reconvene with the next RC-id: proposed features or acceptance items (also listed in the PR body per step 10), low or accepted security findings, deferred follow-ups, unverified assumptions, and actions the user must take. Give each a kind (decision, follow-up or user-action), topic, detail, source (PR, issue or session URI), raised date, affects and status 'open'. Reconvene items never block work; an item the user settles moves to confirmed_by_user (or becomes a feature) and its status becomes 'resolved' with a note. Before reporting in step 11, check that your session's items are recorded.
local_safety: This Mac runs the orch you are changing. Exercise install changes with a temporary --home only; never write to the real ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini, ~/.config/orch, or any repo's git hooks.

Don't restart or replace the running orchd, and don't run `orch install` for real. For anything that needs a daemon or Qdrant, use a separate ORCH_CONFIG_DIR, ORCH_DATA_DIR, socket and Qdrant collection, and remove them when finished.
To capture harness payloads (SP-001), use project-local hook settings in a scratch repository and ask the user before launching each harness session.
Never read, print or store credentials. Use `gh auth status` only; never `gh auth token` or token files.
